name: Second Battle of Tarain
description: A decisive battle that ended Chauhan power at Delhi and opened North India to the Delhi Sultanate.
significance: After Prithviraj's victory in 1191, the second encounter reversed the outcome. The defeat reshaped the politics of the Indo-Gangetic plain.

name: Battle of Khanwa
description: A pivotal battle that established early Mughal dominance over North India after defeating the Rajput confederacy.
significance: Khanwa confirmed that Panipat was not a passing raid. Mughal field artillery and tactics overcame a large Rajput coalition led by Mewar.

name: Second Battle of Panipat
description: A turning point that secured Mughal restoration in India after the challenge of Hemu.
significance: Hemu had seized Delhi; his fall at Panipat allowed the young Akbar's regime to reclaim northern supremacy.

name: Battle of Pratapgad
description: A meeting turned battle in which Shivaji defeated the Bijapur general Afzal Khan and secured a crucial early victory.
significance: Pratapgad announced Maratha military confidence in the Sahyadris and became a founding episode of swarajya.

name: Battle of Sinhagad
description: A night assault that recaptured the fort of Kondhana, later named Sinhagad, at a heavy personal cost.
significance: The recapture of the fort restored a vital western stronghold and entered Maratha memory through Tanaji's sacrifice.

name: Battle of Haldighati
result: Tactical Mughal advantage; Mewar continued resistance
description: A legendary confrontation between Maharana Pratap and Mughal forces in the narrow pass of Haldighati.
significance: Though Pratap withdrew, he never submitted. Haldighati became a symbol of Rajput honour and unfinished resistance.

name: Battle of Dewair
description: A campaign in which Maharana Pratap recovered large parts of Mewar after years of guerrilla war.
significance: Dewair showed that Haldighati was not the end. Mewar clawed back territory and kept Sisodia independence alive.

name: Battle of Saraighat
description: A decisive naval battle where Ahom forces under Lachit Borphukan repelled a Mughal invasion.
significance: Saraighat preserved Assam's independence and stands as one of India's great riverine victories.

name: Battle of Attock
description: A campaign that brought the fortress of Attock under Maharaja Ranjit Singh and opened the northwest.
significance: Attock was a gateway of the Indus. Its capture marked the Sikh Empire as a power on the imperial northwest road.

name: Siege of Jhansi
commanders: Rani Lakshmibai • East India Company forces
description: The siege in which Rani Lakshmibai defended Jhansi Fort during the revolt of 1857–58.
significance: The defense of Jhansi became a defining episode of 1857 and immortalized Lakshmibai as a warrior queen.
